penalties_applied.name: b2c_at_scale_needed
penalties_applied.reason: Target segment is individual consumers and general office workers; the business model requires many small paying users to generate meaningful revenue — typical paid conversion rates in this segment are very low and the market is already served by free tools (LibreOffice Calc, online converters).

rationale: The buyer here is individual data analysts and office workers — a consumer-adjacent segment that overwhelmingly uses free tools (Excel itself opens CSV, LibreOffice is free, dozens of free online converters exist). There is very little evidence of willingness to pay for a standalone CSV-to-Excel converter; paid substitutes at meaningful price points are absent. Operational autonomy is moderate (a downloadable tool or simple web service could run unattended) but the distribution and monetization problem is severe — reaching paying users at scale in a commoditised market is hard without a significant acquisition budget. Not the right fit.
solution_plan: This would be a lightweight web service where users upload a CSV and download a clean Excel file. Claude could handle some data-cleaning logic. However, the market is saturated with free tools, making it nearly impossible to charge meaningfully without a clear differentiator (e.g. a privacy-first offline app would need a desktop installer the factory cannot build). A solo non-technical operator cannot realistically acquire paying customers here at viable unit economics. Drop this one.
notes: Total 3.6 is below min_total_to_validate (5.5). buyer_clarity floor unmet (5, min 6). willingness_to_pay floor unmet (4, min 5).
